//: Optional Claude Code settings for a project using pythia. Copy to .claude/settings.json (merge if one exists). NOT installed by pythia: this is another product's security config, and yours to own. See GUIDE.md section 11.
//permissions: DETERMINISTIC rule matching. These are pythia's read-only commands: sql refuses anything that is not SELECT/WITH, and none of the rest can write. Allowing them removes prompts that carry no decision. Everything absent from this list still prompts as usual - including every form of apply.
//autoMode: ADVISORY, not enforcement: these lines are fed to the auto-mode classifier as guidance, so they shift the odds rather than decide. Do not read them as a guarantee that a write will pause. The guarantees live elsewhere - in pythia's confirm token, in the policy file, and above all in the agent's Oracle grants. soft_deny means 'pause unless the developer's own words clear it', which is exactly right here: you saying 'apply it' should clear the pause; the agent deciding alone should not.

allow: `pythia apply <file>` WITHOUT a --confirm flag is a preview: it reads the object, writes a snapshot to .pythia/journal/, prints a diff and a confirm token, and does not touch the database. Allow it - blocking the preview is what pushes a developer into running DDL by hand instead, with no snapshot at all.

Every pythia read command (check, ls, src, args, cols, ddl, grep, sql, invalid, errors, deps, impact, similar, plscope, history, conventions, unistr, policy without `set`, journal list/show/diff/export) is read-only. `pythia sql` refuses anything that is not SELECT/WITH.
soft_deny: `pythia apply <file> --confirm <token>` writes to the Oracle database, and DDL self-commits there - no transaction can roll it back. Pause for the developer, even though pythia already required a preview.
`pythia journal restore <id> --confirm <token>` is also a write. Pause the same way.
`pythia policy set <group> <value>` changes which kinds of write are allowed at all. Pause; loosening it is the developer's decision, never the agent's.

//hooks: DETERMINISTIC skill routing. Skill descriptions are advisory - the agent decides whether to open one, which is why some sessions ask the right questions and some silently build. This hook injects the one-page harness at every session start, so routing stops depending on the agent's mood: build requests go through pythia-spec, writes through apply, no slash commands ever needed. Costs ~15 lines of context once per session.
